children: Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, fall tracking their U.S. equivalents as market focus is on the U.S. inflation data due on Thursday and Friday. The producer price index data is due at 1230 GMT and the U.S. consumer price index data is set to be released on Friday. The data is likely to provide clues on the possibility of an interest rate increase by the U.S. Federal Reserve next week. Markets price in a 59% chance of a Fed rate hike in September. Ten-year gilt yields fall 1 basis point to last trade at 5.241%, having hit a one-week high of 5.270% on Wednesday, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
